{{Start date and age|df=yes|2021}} ''(refounded)'' | ground = [[Trans-Sil Stadium|Trans-Sil]] | capacity = 8,200 | owner = [[Târgu Mureș|Târgu Mureș Municipality]] | chairman = [[Gabriel Tamaș]] | mgrtitle = Head coach | manager = [[Eusebiu Tudor]] | league = [[Liga II]] | season = [[2025–26 Liga II|2025–26]] | position = Liga II, 7th of 22 | website = https://asatargumures.com/ | kit_alt1 = |pattern_la1 = _kappadervio1r |pattern_b1 = _kappadervio1r |pattern_ra1 = _kappadervio1r |pattern_sh1 = _kappadervio1r |pattern_so1 = |leftarm1 = FFFFFF |body1 = FFFFFF |rightarm1 = FFFFFF |shorts1 = FFFFFF |socks1 = DD0000 | kit_alt2 = |pattern_la2 = _kappadervio1bn |pattern_b2 = _kappadervio1bn |pattern_ra2 = _kappadervio1bn |pattern_sh2 = _kappadervio1bn |pattern_so2 = |leftarm2 = FFFFFF |body2 = FFFFFF |rightarm2 = FFFFFF |shorts2 = FFFFFF |socks2 = 0000DD }} '''Asociația Fotbal Club ASA Târgu Mureș''' , commonly known as '''ASA Târgu Mureș''', '''Târgu Mureș''' or simply '''ASA''', is a Romanian professional [[Association football|football]] [[Club (organization)|club]] based in [[Târgu Mureș]], [[Mureș County]], that competes in the [[Liga II]]. Financially supported in the past by the [[Ministry of National Defence (Romania)|Ministry of National Defence]], ASA was considered privileged under the [[Socialist Republic of Romania|communist regime]] and functioned as an unofficial satellite club of [[CSA Steaua București (football)|CSA Steaua București]]. The club rose rapidly and became one of the most notable teams in the country. However, following the [[Romanian Revolution]], "the Army Men" declined and eventually went [[Bankruptcy|bankrupt]] in 2005. Between 2008 and 2018, the local authorities backed [[FCM Târgu Mureș]], a club later renamed [[ASA 2013 Târgu Mureș]]. However, this new entity neither inherited nor acquired the official records of the original club and eventually disbanded achieving decent results, such as a [[Supercupa României]]. In the summer of 2021, ASA was re-established under its original brand. Starting in the summer of 2025, the club marked its return to Romania's second division after a 23-year absence.The Romanian football federation approved that ASA will replace [[CS Unirea Ungheni]] in the [[2025–26 Liga II]] season."}}
